sections.title: Start without money or a "brilliant idea"

items.q: What should you start a business with if not an original idea?
items.a: **What you love doing** plus a revenue model to experiment with. Fluid had **500 Hong Kong competitors**; Squibb won through obsession with marketing, not novelty. First steps should be cheap: podcast, blog, LinkedIn post.

items.q: Why prefer a mind map over a business plan?
items.a: Mind maps **cost nothing and stay liquid**; business plans **ossify and kill exploration**. Stay nimble from hobby → business instead of locking a rigid plan early.

items.q: How does the free-first-customer strategy work?
items.a: Fluid's first client got work **free** — over-deliver → a **16-year relationship** plus referrals. **Bring value before extracting money**; delayed gratification is the **#1 win lever**.

items.q: How is luck "hackable" according to Squibb?
items.a: Stack **persistence** (outlast competitors), a **defined destination** (his success = school pickup + exercise, not a yacht), and **positioning in opportunity's path**. Luck isn't subjective — it's engineered.

items.q: Why must entrepreneurs learn to accept losing everything?
items.a: **Detach from things owning you** so you can risk without paralysis. Failure is recoverable; accepting total loss unlocks the stamina to win the marathon.

items.q: How should you choose a co-founder?
items.a: **Opposite skills + shared values.** Prefer **50% of a business you enjoy** over **100% of a nightmare**. Equity structure matters early.

items.q: What does long-game sales look like?
items.a: **Monthly touchpoints for years** — some Fluid clients took **9 years**. An **email list** still beats TikTok coolness for B2B conversion over time.

items.q: What is the seven-and-eight hiring rule?
items.a: **Fire mediocre performers** or your **nines and tens leave**. Hire for purpose (check social + references) and **give employees equity**.

items.q: How does Squibb sequence funding without early valuation fights?
items.a: Ladder: friends/family (tell the truth — could lose all) → angels (never beg like Dragon's Den) → VC later → crowdfunding for **pre-sales without equity dilution**. YC **SAFE** defers valuation fights.

items.q: How do natural brand sponsorships happen?
items.a: Use products you **actually love** (Ring, Whoop); brands come to you. Marketing should be **fun** — Starbucks made the store the billboard.

items.q: What's the strongest way to sell a company?
items.a: **"The best way to sell your company is not want to sell it at all."** Partner with the acquirer first (Fluid → PwC); non-industry buyers can pay more; reverse-engineer equity from the end goal on day one.
